children: shares edged higher Tuesday after an 18.5% plunge a day earlier, as Wall Street analysts tried to separate near-term leadership uncertainty from what they still see as a strong long-term growth story.
The selloff followed the departure of CEO Chirantan CJ Desai, who is leaving MongoDB to join Meta Platforms

DA Davidson analyst Rudy Kessinger called the departure very disappointing, pointing to Desai's importance in strengthening MongoDB's relationships with large enterprise customers and helping the company win bigger, longer-duration deals.
Kessinger nevertheless kept a Buy rating and $465 price target on MDB, implying more than 38% upside from the level cited in the report.
MongoDB has brought back longtime executive Dev Ittycheria as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Ittycheria previously led the company from 2014 through 2025.
The timing of the transition has made the situation more sensitive.
Desai's departure came just ahead of MongoDB's Investor Day in New York City, where management is expected to lay out its growth strategy and longer-term priorities.
Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda said the timing was clearly negative and complicates the setup, adding uncertainty around strategy, leadership and execution.

Still, Ikeda argued that Ittycheria could provide more stability than a typical interim CEO given his long history with MongoDB. He maintained a Buy rating and $540 price target, implying more than 60% upside.
The immediate risk for MongoDB investors is not the product story, but execution during a leadership transition.
Desai's exit could disrupt enterprise relationships or complicate near-term messaging at Investor Day. But analysts are not abandoning the stock.
That makes Tuesday's rebound important to watch. If management can reassure investors on succession, customer momentum and strategy, the 18% drop could begin to look overdone.
But any sign that leadership uncertainty is spilling into sales execution would make the selloff harder to dismiss.

title: DA Davidson Has A Message For MongoDB Stock Investors
